justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift across time horizons, starting near 32.15 for the one-day forecast and edging toward 32.5 at one month. This trajectory likely reflects a baseline assumption of slight positive momentum or mean-reversion toward a near-term fair value, anchored heavily by recent price action and short-term technical levels. At the one-day horizon, the estimate is tightly anchored to the last observed price, with very little room built in for directional movement since overnight sessions and intraday catalysts tend to produce only marginal net displacement on average. As the horizon extends to one week and one month, I incorporated a small positive drift assumption — consistent with a modest risk premium or bullish bias in the underlying trend — while acknowledging that the compounding of daily uncertainty naturally widens the range of plausible outcomes.

The confidence interval widths grow substantially as the horizon lengthens, and this reflects the well-established principle that uncertainty compounds over time. At one day, the 90% interval spans roughly 2.1 units, which corresponds to a tight range driven primarily by short-term volatility clustering — recent realized volatility being low enough to constrain near-term swings. By one week, the interval widens to 4.6 units, incorporating the possibility of moderate news-driven moves or shifts in market sentiment. At one month, the interval opens to a full 10 units, reflecting structural uncertainty about macroeconomic data releases, central bank communication, earnings, or geopolitical developments that could materially reprice the asset. Implied or historical volatility scaling (roughly proportional to the square root of time) is the primary mechanical driver of this widening.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside even these wide intervals. A sudden liquidity shock, an unexpected policy announcement, or a geopolitical escalation could produce gap moves that sit well beyond the 90% bounds at any horizon. On the upside, a stronger-than-expected fundamental catalyst — such as a surprise earnings beat, a policy pivot, or a short squeeze dynamic — could push prices above 37.5 at the one-month horizon. On the downside, a risk-off episode, a credit event, or deteriorating macro data could drive prices below 27.5. These tail risks are real but deliberately excluded from the 90% interval by construction — they represent the 10% of outcomes I judged plausible but not central to the forecast distribution.
